subject.title: Feature: Inter-session progress streaming for sessions_send (ACP/long-running session support)

question: Should OpenClaw define a core caller-readable run-progress observation contract for `sessions_send` now, and should it be exposed as `sessions_subscribe`, a `sessions_send` option, or a broader process-event API?
rationale: The choice creates an observable gateway/session event contract and can expose intermediate tool, assistant, ACP, command, or artifact data, so automation should not pick the schema, retention, authorization, or redaction model alone.

options.title: Design Core Subscription Contract
options.body: Approve a scoped run-event read or subscription API with explicit authorization, redaction, buffering, replay, retention, and channel-delivery rules before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Process Events
options.body: Treat this as one consumer of the broader structured process/step event work and avoid a sessions_send-specific API until that contract is chosen.

options.title: Defer Beyond Completion Paths
options.body: Keep the existing accepted/final-announce behavior and defer live inter-session progress until a stronger product need or API owner emerges.

recommendation.title: Design Core Subscription Contract
recommendation.body: Approve a scoped run-event read or subscription API with explicit authorization, redaction, buffering, replay, retention, and channel-delivery rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across sessions_send, run-wait, A2A, and structured event surfaces, and this decision is primarily about the permanent core progress contract.
